result.summary:
Read git diff main...HEAD directly (24 files, 3416 insertions/15 deletions per `git diff --stat`), not MOBILE-DEV's or SECURITY-REVIEWER's summaries.

1. IDIOMATIC vs. CRUTCH.
- TenantTokenStore.production() (apps/mobile/lib/auth/auth.dart): a plain factory constructor wrapping FlutterSecureStorage with named AndroidOptions()/IOSOptions(accessibility:...) — standard Dart factory-constructor idiom for a hardened production configuration, no reflection/codegen/singleton smell. The package-version deviation (AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences:true) removed in v11) is documented inline with the same convention RealAppAuthAdapter already uses elsewhere in this codebase — consistent, not ad hoc.
- transport_policy.dart: TransportPolicy as an abstract interface with Release/Debug implementations and a factory function (transportPolicyFor) is textbook strategy-pattern Dart — small, immutable (@immutable, const constructors), trivially testable by injecting the policy instead of reading kReleaseMode internally. Idiomatic.
- MaskRevealController/MaskedRevealText (design_system/masked_text.dart): a ChangeNotifier-based 3-phase enum state machine (masked -> revealed -> locked, one-directional, no-op on invalid transition) driving a StatelessWidget via ListenableBuilder. This is the correct Flutter idiom for this exact shape of ephemeral, non-persisted UI state — no crutch (e.g. no bool flags standing in for a state machine, no setState-on-a-StatefulWidget doing what ChangeNotifier already does cleanly).
- RedactingLogInterceptor: a Dio Interceptor subclass with injectable logSink (defaulting to debugPrint via a documented top-level forwarding function, since debugPrint itself isn't a compile-time constant) — standard Dio interceptor-chain idiom, correctly left unregistered per design OQ-1 rather than force-wired in ahead of an actual need (REQ-425/MOB-6). This is right-sized: infrastructure built when its interface is needed, not wired in before there's a caller.
- Tear-off delegation (_switchTenantTopLevel/_logoutTopLevel in navigation_bootstrap.dart): this is the one item worth a substantive idiom note. The mechanism is correct Dart (module-scope tear-offs resolve unambiguously and capture no instance state, as SECURITY-REVIEWER independently confirmed) and it is unusually well-documented (the doc comments on the two tear-off variables and both class methods all explain the same-name resolution hazard). But re-declaring the full parameter signature a second time as a function-typed top-level variable (once as `logout({required TenantTokenStore tokenStore, ...})`, again as `final Future<void> Function({required TenantTokenStore tokenStore, ...}) _logoutTopLevel = logout;`) is more surface area to keep in sync than the problem needs — a same-named top-level function colliding with a same-named instance method is conventionally resolved in Dart/Flutter code by renaming one of the two (e.g. top-level `logoutTenant`/`switchToTenant`, or controller methods `performLogout`/`performSwitchTenant`), which needs no shadow variable and no second signature to maintain. This is a legitimate, non-blocking style preference, not a functional crutch — flagging it as a note for a future pass rather than blocking this gate, since: (a) the current form is provably correct (verified independently by SECURITY-REVIEWER already), (b) it is thoroughly self-documenting, and (c) forcing a rework cycle for a signature-duplication style nit when the underlying mechanism is sound would not be proportionate to the finding.

2. LIFECYCLE INTEGRITY (Flutter/Riverpod equivalent of supervision).
- tenantTokenStoreProvider is a plain Provider<TenantTokenStore> now calling TenantTokenStore.production() directly (the deleted flutterSecureStorageProvider indirection is gone) — this closes the AC1 'only one file constructs it' requirement cleanly and is the standard Riverpod idiom (a Provider that returns an immutable value, overridable in tests via ProviderScope(overrides:...), documented explicitly in the surrounding comment block as 'the standard Riverpod testing idiom, not a second wiring path').
- No controller or widget holds a stale reference across tenant switch: BootstrapController.switchTenant/.logout both go through the identical activeRealm/tokenStore fields already owned by the controller instance (no new provider scope, no rebuilt controller instance mid-switch) — the controller's own notifyListeners()-driven state (_state) is reassigned synchronously inside each method, so any widget listening via ChangeNotifier sees the transition atomically; there is no window where a widget could read a phase computed against a since-replaced token store. MaskRevealController is explicitly documented as one-instance-per-secret-value ('a screen showing N secrets constructs N controllers') — correct scoping, no shared/singleton controller that would leak reveal-state across unrelated secrets.
- No unsupervised isolate/async gap introduced: switchTenant's extra fetchTenantConfig call and subsequent runTenantBootstrap call are both awaited in sequence inside one async function body, not fired-and-forgotten.

3. TYPE-SAFETY GAPS. No new class of invalid state stood out that a struct/enum change would make unrepresentable and that isn't already handled: MaskRevealPhase is already an enum with an explicit invalid-transition no-op; BootstrapFailureReason is already a typed enum reused (not a new stringly-typed error). Nothing to file under docs/issues/ from this diff.

4. SCOPE CREEP.
- Confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD --stat` filtered against MOBILE-DEV's step-02b-mobile-dev.json artifacts_out list: every changed file falls under apps/mobile/ or docs/mobile/architecture.md, plus this run's own handoffs/ and lib/letflow/design/req422-mobile-security-hardening.md (design doc, not application code) and docs/requirements.yaml/status files (ORCH's own bookkeeping, pre-existing modified files per git status, not part of this diff review). No lib/letflow/ backend code and no web/ file touched — confirmed by the stat output having zero lines under either path.
- No unrelated refactor rode along: every new file/function traces to a specific BUILDS item (1 token store, 2 redaction, 3/3b transport, 4 iOS, 5/6/7 audience+masking+docs) in REQ-422's own requirement text. transport_policy.dart's abstraction (an interface with two implementations rather than a single function with an isRelease bool) is proportionate, not premature: the design and diff both need it injected as a value at two independent call sites (ApiClient interceptor chain and bootstrap's realm_url check) with test doubles at both, which is exactly what an interface earns its keep for at this size — not a case of building general plumbing ahead of the stage's actual need.

DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY: checked docs/migration/decisions/0012-mobile-tier-stack.md and docs/mobile/{README.md,architecture.md,requirements.md,build-order.md} — no contradiction. The diff introduces no new pubspec dependency (confirmed unchanged in the diff stat), no general scripting runtime, no offline-write cache, and tokens are only ever constructed via TenantTokenStore.production()'s OS-secure storage path — consistent with the three-tier mobile constraints in .claude/agents/mobile-dev.md. docs/mobile/architecture.md's new §7 explicitly scopes certificate pinning/root-jailbreak detection as required-before-corporate-tier and not-v1, matching MOB-5's own [S]-priority marking rather than silently deferring without a record.

ANTI-PATTERNS: docs/anti-patterns.md grepped for tear-off/mobile/Riverpod/provider/secure_storage/Dart/Flutter-related entries — no match; nothing in this diff resembles a previously-recorded mistake.

OQ-6 (REQ-421's stale key-rotation/biometric-gating/tamper-detection forward-reference): agree with CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's disposition. REQ-422's own requirement_text and acceptance_criteria (both quoted verbatim in this run's step-02b/step-02c handoffs) contain no such items — this diff's own auth.dart doc-comment change explicitly and correctly narrows the claim ('Key rotation, biometric gating, and tamper detection are not part of REQ-422's requirement text ... and are not implemented here') rather than either fabricating undesigned scope to satisfy a stale forward-reference or silently leaving the discrepancy unrecorded. Demanding those items be added now would itself be scope creep against REQ-422's actual acceptance criteria. This is a documentation-consistency issue belonging to REQ-421, not a REVIEWER gate failure on REQ-422 — non-blocking, leave as ORCH's follow-up per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's recommendation.

No BLOCKER, no rework required. One non-blocking idiom note recorded above (tear-off signature duplication — recommend a future rename-based simplification, not required for this gate).

issues.description: BootstrapController.switchTenant/.logout delegate through module-level tear-off variables (_switchTenantTopLevel/_logoutTopLevel in apps/mobile/lib/bootstrap/navigation_bootstrap.dart) that re-state the full top-level function signature a second time as a function-typed variable, to work around Dart resolving a same-named bare call to the instance member first. Functionally correct and independently verified safe by SECURITY-REVIEWER; the conventional Dart/Flutter idiom for this exact collision is to rename one side (e.g. top-level logoutTenant/switchToTenant, or controller methods performLogout/performSwitchTenant) rather than introduce a shadow variable whose type must be kept in sync with the top-level signature. Recommend MOBILE-DEV apply the rename in a later, low-risk pass; not required for this gate.

Endorsing CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's OQ-6 finding: REQ-421's own text (docs/mobile/ and/or lib/letflow/design/req421-mobile-tenant-bootstrap.md) forward-references key rotation/biometric gating/tamper detection as REQ-422 scope; REQ-422's actual requirement text/acceptance criteria contain none of these, and this diff's own updated doc comment in auth.dart correctly narrows the claim instead of silently absorbing or dropping it. This is REQ-421's stale reference to correct, not a REQ-422 gap — recommend ORCH file the follow-up as previously suggested; does not block this gate.
